Forward-looking statements in this annual report include statements about clinical development, regulatory timing, financing needs, strategic alternatives, and Nasdaq compliance. Actual results may differ materially.
PART I
ITEM 1. Business
Nova Therapeutics Inc. develops implantable metabolic therapies. In 2024 the company launched a new product platform for its metabolic monitoring device and continued a Phase 2 clinical trial under an active IND. Management also began evaluating strategic alternatives, including a possible asset sale or partnership for the monitoring business.
ITEM 1A. Risk Factors
On August 30, 2024, the company received a letter from Nasdaq notifying it that the bid price of its common stock had closed below the $1.00 per share minimum bid price required for continued listing on the Nasdaq Capital Market. The company has until September 15, 2025 to regain compliance. Our recurring losses and negative operating cash flows raise substantial doubt about our ability to continue as a going concern. We will require additional capital to fund operations through the next twelve months.
ITEM 1B. Unresolved Staff Comments
None.
ITEM 1C. Cybersecurity
The board oversees cybersecurity risk management. The company did not identify a material cybersecurity incident during 2024, but cybersecurity risk management remains part of enterprise risk oversight.
ITEM 3. Legal Proceedings
The company received a subpoena from the SEC staff concerning prior revenue recognition practices and is cooperating with the investigation. A related securities class action lawsuit remains pending in federal court.
PART II
ITEM 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations
Revenue decreased by 42.0% to $18.0 million from $31.0 million due to lower device placements. Net loss was $86.0 million compared with $54.0 million in the prior year. Cash and cash equivalents 12.0 44.0. Total debt 58.0 32.0. Working capital deficit was $21.0 million at December 31, 2024. The company was not in compliance with a debt covenant as of year end and obtained a limited waiver of default after year end.

ITEM 9A. Controls and Procedures
Management identified material weaknesses in internal control over financial reporting related to revenue recognition, segregation of duties, and review of complex debt accounting. Disclosure controls and procedures were not effective as of December 31, 2024.
